channel.title: Guides: CapitalVerdict
channel.description: Plain-language guides to big money decisions in India, worked through with the same maths as the CapitalVerdict calculators.

item.title: Car loan or cash: what the loan really costs
item.description: A car loan is worth taking only if your savings earn more than the loan really costs. With a processing fee, that is more than the quoted rate. And a flat rate hides the real one. Worked examples.

item.title: Your FD's real return after tax and inflation
item.description: A 7% fixed deposit sounds safe and steady. After tax at the higher slabs and 6% inflation, it can lose buying power every year. Here is the arithmetic for each slab.

item.title: How mutual fund gains are taxed in 2026: short-term, long-term and the ₹1.25 lakh exemption
item.description: Equity fund gains are taxed when you sell, at 20% if held a year or less and 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh a year if held longer. Worked examples, including a SIP.

item.title: Is income up to ₹12 lakh really tax-free? The rebate and marginal relief
item.description: Under the new regime, taxable income up to ₹12 lakh pays no tax, and a salary up to ₹12.75 lakh with it. Just above, marginal relief stops the tax jumping. Here is the arithmetic.

item.title: Is a 5-star inverter AC worth the extra price?
item.description: An efficient AC saves electricity every summer, but costs more up front. Whether it pays back depends mostly on how much you run it. Worked through with the star label's own numbers.

item.title: After prepaying: lower the EMI or shorten the loan?
item.description: When you prepay a home loan, the bank asks whether to cut your EMI or the number of EMIs. Keeping the EMI saves far more interest. Here is by how much, and when lowering the EMI still makes sense.

item.title: Old or new tax regime for 2026-27: who should switch
item.description: The new regime is the default and often wins. The old one wins only above a certain level of deductions. Here is how to find yours, with worked examples.

item.title: Plot vs mutual fund: the costs plot buyers forget
item.description: A plot's price may double, but stamp duty, holding costs, selling costs and tax take a large share. Compared with an FD and an equity fund, a ₹20 lakh plot needs to grow over 11% a year to keep up.

item.title: Should you prepay your home loan or invest the money?
item.description: Prepaying earns exactly your loan rate, risk-free. Investing has to beat that after tax. Worked through for a ₹40 lakh loan with ₹5 lakh to spare, including the effect of a tax deduction.

item.title: SIP vs PPF: what ₹10,000 a month leaves you after 15 years
item.description: PPF is tax-free and certain; an equity SIP can grow more but is taxed and can fall. Compared after tax, the SIP needs a fund return above about 7.8% a year to come out ahead.

item.title: Break-even: the one number to ask for
item.description: Whenever you pay more now to save later, ask how many months it takes to get the extra back, counting what that money could have earned.

item.title: Is rooftop solar worth it? Start with your own bill
item.description: Rooftop solar pays back through the units it saves you from buying. How fast depends on your bill, your tariff slab and what happens to units you export.

item.title: Lucknow CNG now ₹107 a kg
item.description: Green Gas Limited's price page lists CNG in Lucknow at ₹107.00 a kg from 3 October 2026. Here is what it does to the CNG car's payback.

item.title: Rent or buy: the maths most people skip
item.description: Comparing EMI with rent misses half the picture. A fair comparison follows both households and invests whatever the cheaper one saves.

item.title: Why ₹1 crore in 15 years is less than it sounds
item.description: Future amounts look large because prices rise in the meantime. Converting them to today's rupees makes long-term comparisons honest.

item.title: When does a CNG car pay back?
item.description: A CNG car costs more to buy and less to run. Here is how to work out when the saving covers the extra price, and when it never does.

item.title: Where your EMI goes
item.description: In the early years of a home loan most of each EMI is interest. Here is the arithmetic, and what a yearly prepayment does to it.
